question: What is an ethical dilemma in midwifery practice?

options.A: A situation where two competing moral principles apply with no easy choice
options.B: A disagreement between a patient and doctor about medication costs
options.C: An equipment failure that delays emergency surgical delivery
options.D: A clear violation of hospital rules by a nursing staff member

explanation: An ethical dilemma happens when you are caught between competing moral duties, making any choice carry a difficult ethical weight. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are ethical dilemmas different from simple technical mistakes in the labour ward?

options.A: They involve conflicting values rather than a lack of clinical skill
options.B: They can always be resolved by checking the hospital manual
options.C: They only happen when senior doctors are absent from the ward
options.D: They carry no legal consequences for the attending midwife

explanation: Technical errors happen due to a procedure or knowledge gap, while ethical dilemmas challenge your core values and professional duties. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which principle requires a midwife to actively promote the health and well-being of a mother and newborn?
explanation: Beneficence is the active duty to do good and secure the best possible health outcomes for the patient. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does the principle of non-maleficence apply during a complicated childbirth?

options.A: It forces the midwife to tell the complete truth about birth complications
options.B: It requires the midwife to avoid causing unnecessary harm or injury to mother and baby
options.C: It gives the mother absolute power to refuse any medical intervention offered
options.D: It ensures that rich and poor patients receive the exact same hospital bed

explanation: Non-maleficence focuses on the core rule to do no harm and protect the patient from preventable risks. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is a common ethical conflict in busy maternity units?

options.A: A midwife forgetting to document the exact time of placental delivery
options.B: A labouring woman refusing a life-saving caesarean section
options.C: A hospital running out of clean linen for postnatal ward beds
options.D: A student nurse arriving late for the morning handover meeting

explanation: Refusing life-saving care creates a difficult clash between respecting patient autonomy and fulfilling the duty of beneficence. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h3)

question: A midwife has only one available oxygen cylinder for two asphyxiated newborns. Which ethical principle is tested here?
explanation: Distributing scarce medical resources fairly among competing patients is the core focus of the principle of justice. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a midwife when a competent pregnant patient refuses treatment?

options.A: Call the hospital security team to restrain the patient for her own safety
options.B: Ensure she understands the risks of her choice and document the discussion fully
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately without giving any further care
options.D: Ignore her wishes and carry out the treatment anyway to save the baby

explanation: Respecting autonomy means a competent adult can refuse care, provided they are fully informed of the risks and the discussion is documented. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which practice is unacceptable when trying to convince a patient to accept medical care?

options.A: Consulting a senior obstetrician for advice
options.B: Explaining the clinical risks of refusing treatment
options.C: Involving family members in supportive counseling
options.D: Using coercion or threats to force compliance

explanation: Coercion destroys genuine informed consent and violates both human rights and professional standards. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the first step a midwife should take when facing an ethical dilemma?

options.A: Ask the hospital chaplain to convince the patient to change her mind
options.B: Immediately report the patient to the hospital legal department
options.C: Follow the senior doctor's orders without asking any questions
options.D: Clearly identify the core conflict and competing principles

explanation: An ethical problem cannot be solved until you clearly define what values and principles are in conflict. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is consulting colleagues an important step in ethical decision-making?

options.A: It ensures the midwife bears no personal blame if the patient dies
options.B: It speeds up the labour process for the woman in distress
options.C: It legally transfers the responsibility of care to the hospital board
options.D: It brings diverse perspectives and helps reduce individual bias

explanation: Collaborative discussion helps clinicians see blind spots and ensures decisions are balanced rather than rushed. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which body in Nigeria has the power to discipline midwives and regulate professional practice?

options.B: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the legal regulatory body responsible for setting standards, training, and disciplining midwives in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the key difference between ethical codes and legal regulations in midwifery?

options.A: Legal regulations have no penalties, whereas breaking ethical codes leads to immediate jail time
options.B: There is no difference; every ethical rule is also an enforceable criminal law
options.C: Legal regulations set minimum mandatory standards, whereas ethical codes guide ideal moral behavior
options.D: Ethical codes are written down by judges, while laws are created by hospital matrons

explanation: Laws are mandatory rules backed by state punishment, while ethics represent the moral ideals of the profession. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of peer debriefing sessions in a busy maternity unit?

options.A: To punish junior midwives who make documentation errors on the night shift
options.B: To teach medical students advanced surgical procedures for emergency delivery
options.C: To evaluate how many patients each nurse admitted during the month
options.D: To provide a safe space for staff to discuss traumatic cases and emotional distress

explanation: Peer debriefing helps clinicians process the emotional burden of difficult cases, preventing burnout. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h7)

question: How does reflective practice primarily benefit a professional midwife over time?

options.A: It reduces the number of night shifts she is assigned by the matron
options.B: It helps her learn from past clinical experiences to improve future decision-making
options.C: It legally protects her from being sued by patients in family courts
options.D: It guarantees that she will never face another ethical dilemma in her career

explanation: Reflection turns everyday clinical experiences into deep professional learning, sharpening both technical and ethical judgment. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T1#BMP127_U3_T1_h7)
